vision: Find or construct a labeled corpus where each record is a planned intervention (change, deployment, release, commit) with structured pre-execution attributes and a verifiable post-execution failure outcome — not an 'ITSM dataset' but any domain that instantiates the abstract question: 'Given what we know before execution, will this cause a failure?' Success is a tiered shortlist (gold/silver/bronze/constructed) with honest sample sizes, label quality, and a clear mapping to which pipeline stages each dataset can validate. BPI 2014 is one candidate among many, not the default answer.
direction: Reframe the search around an abstract Intervention→Outcome schema (intervention_id, scope, type, risk, schedule, optional prose artifacts → failure severity, timestamp, linkage quality). Run domain-parallel searches across software engineering (JIT/SZZ), process mining (all BPI + XES), DevOps/SRE (deployments, rollbacks, CFR), release engineering, and industrial change control — using domain-native vocabulary, not ITSM keywords. Apply a tiered label-quality framework (direct link → temporal+scope → proxy label → constructed join) instead of a binary deal-breaker. For each hit, score: mappable fields, positive-class n, temporal split viability, artifact richness, license. End with a synthesis that ranks options by validation goal (architecture vs predictive vs full 9-stage), explicitly challenging whether we need ITSM fidelity or can validate the risk-prediction thesis on adjacent domains and transfer learnings back.

trade_offs.decision: Tiered label quality (A/B/C/D) instead of binary direct-linkage deal-breaker
trade_offs.alternative: Keep v1 rule: discard unless explicit change→incident field populated
trade_offs.reasoning: Direct linkage is rare (<5% even in enterprise ITSM per ING/BPI). Temporal+scope linkage (incident on same service within N hours post-change) yields 10–100× more labels at the cost of false positives. Proxy labels (SZZ bug-inducing commits) have different semantics but support predictive model benchmarking at scale. We gain statistical power; we lose ITSM-specific causal certainty.

trade_offs.decision: Validate predictive thesis on adjacent domains (JIT defect, deployment failure) if ITSM gold data absent
trade_offs.alternative: Wait for enterprise ITSM partner before any predictive eval
trade_offs.reasoning: The pipeline's core ML question — 'does historical pattern + completeness signal predict failure?' — is domain-agnostic. JIT datasets offer 10K–100K labeled interventions with rich text. We lose runbook/rollback/CAB semantics and must build domain-specific adapters, but gain defensible precision/recall metrics. Transfer back to ITSM is hypothesis, not proven.

trade_offs.decision: Pursue constructed datasets (GitHub deploy events + incident issues + postmortems) as first-class path
trade_offs.reasoning: No public monolith combines ITSM structure + incident outcomes + prose artifacts. Construction via temporal joins is labor-intensive but may be the only path to silver-tier ITSM-like labels at scale. Risk: join assumptions become hidden bias; must document and sensitivity-test window sizes.

trade_offs.decision: Accept partial pipeline validation per dataset tier
trade_offs.alternative: Require all 9 stages exercisable on one dataset
trade_offs.reasoning: Prose artifacts (runbook, rollback) essentially do not exist in public real data. Synthetic fixtures already cover stages 4/5/7. Real-data eval should target stages 1–3, 6, 8–9 on structured data; treat 4/5/7 as synthetic-only until enterprise partner. Trying to find one dataset for all 9 stages guarantees failure.

trade_offs.decision: Exhaust non-ITSM sources before re-ranking BPI 2014
trade_offs.alternative: Treat BPI 2014 as confirmed best and run PoC immediately
trade_offs.reasoning: v1 search was keyword-biased toward ITSM platforms. Adjacent domains may offer better predictive validation even if adapter work is higher. BPI remains valuable as the only real ITIL event log — but its n=25 P1/P2 positives may be beatable by SZZ or deployment datasets for the ML thesis.

trade_offs.decision: Contact authors of private datasets (ING/Kapel) for academic access
trade_offs.reasoning: ING paper matches our problem exactly (175K changes, 4K incident-inducing). Low probability of success but high value; costs one email. Does not block parallel public search.

open_questions: Validation goal priority: (A) prove pipeline architecture on real ITIL shapes, (B) prove predictive accuracy with statistical power, or (C) exercise all 9 stages including prose artifacts? These require different datasets — which is P0?
Acceptable label noise for predictive eval: what false-positive rate in silver-tier temporal linkage is tolerable (e.g., incident within 24h on same service ≠ caused by change)?
Is validating on JIT defect prediction (commit→bug) sufficient evidence for CAB risk prediction, or is that a different product claim requiring ITSM-specific eval?
Budget for dataset construction: person-days cap for GitHub/API scraping and temporal joins vs buying commercial process-mining samples?
P1/P2 severity only (ING-style) or any-severity incidents as positive class? Broader definition increases n but dilutes CAB-relevant signal.
Should we pursue Data Use Agreements with Rabobank successors, ING, or BPI challenge organizers for richer extracts beyond public BPI 2014?
If best public option remains BPI 2014, do we proceed with PoC knowing n=25, or pivot MVP claims to 'architecture validated, predictive accuracy unmeasured' until enterprise data?

tasks.title: Reframe problem + tiered acceptance criteria
tasks.scope: Define the abstract Intervention→Outcome schema, map each pipeline stage to minimum data requirements, and replace v1 binary deal-breakers with Tier A/B/C/D label quality levels. Produce a one-page rubric used by all subsequent search tasks. Does NOT search yet — sets the lens.
acceptance_criteria: Abstract schema documented: intervention fields, outcome fields, linkage types, temporal split rules
Tier A/B/C/D definitions with examples from ITSM, JIT, and DevOps domains
Per-stage minimum data matrix: which stages need which artifacts (1–9)
Three validation modes defined: architecture-only, predictive, full-pipeline
Explicit list of what v1 got wrong (keyword bias, binary deal-breaker, BPI anchoring)

search_strategy.hit_criteria: Rubric artifact ready for downstream tasks — no external search

tasks.title: JIT defect prediction + SZZ labeled commit corpora
tasks.scope: Search software-engineering datasets where code changes (commits/PRs) are labeled bug-inducing vs clean. Largest public corpora for predictive validation at scale. Assess adapter feasibility to CRBundle (commit message ≈ description, files ≈ affected_services, author metrics ≈ team features).
acceptance_criteria: ≥5 datasets catalogued with size, label method (SZZ/manual), positive-class n, license
Top 2 candidates scored against tier rubric and pipeline stage coverage
Honest assessment: does bug-inducing ≡ incident-causing for our thesis?
Adapter sketch: which CRBundle fields map, which stages activate/skip

search_strategy.hit_criteria: Labeled commits or PRs (≥1K positive class) with pre-change features (diff stats, author, timestamp, message) and binary/multiclass defect outcome. Manual labels preferred over pure SZZ; document label noise if SZZ-only.

tasks.title: DevOps / SRE deployment and rollback failure datasets
tasks.scope: Search for deployment/release records linked to failures, rollbacks, or incidents. Closer semantic match to ITSM changes than commits — planned execution with scope and schedule.
acceptance_criteria: ≥5 candidates from CI/CD, cloud outage, and DORA research corpora
Each assessed: deployment fields, failure definition, linkage method, n
Flag any dataset with rollback events as proxy for 'change caused failure'
Note GitHub deployment API + issues as construction path if no monolith found

search_strategy.hit_criteria: Deployment/release record with timestamp, target service/repo, outcome (success/failure/rollback) OR linked incident within documented window. Tier B acceptable if same-service temporal join is explicit.

tasks.title: Process mining event logs — all BPI challenges + XES repository
tasks.scope: Systematic crawl of ALL BPI Challenge years (2012–2022) and the IEEE/XES process mining archive — not just 2014. Many years include incident/problem/change subprocesses under non-ITSM names.
acceptance_criteria: Inventory table: every BPI year, domain, log objects, case counts, ITIL relevance score
Non-BPI XES logs with incident/change/problem lifecycle identified (≥10 inspected)
Any log with both change-like and incident-like events scored for Tier A/B linkage
BPI 2014 re-assessed with tier framework — not assumed rank #1

platforms: IEEE Task Force on Process Mining (xes-standard.org)
search_strategy.hit_criteria: Event log with ≥2 activity types mappable to intervention (change/deploy/release) and outcome (incident/failure/ticket escalation), ideally same case ID or documented cross-case join key. Minimum 500 intervention cases.

tasks.title: Release engineering + configuration change failure corpora
tasks.scope: Search release-tracking and config-change domains: failed releases, hotfix-after-release, infrastructure-as-code apply failures, feature-flag rollouts with rollback.
acceptance_criteria: ≥3 candidates with release/change record + post-release failure label
IaC/terraform failure datasets assessed (apply failure ≠ incident but may proxy)
Distinction documented: release failure vs production incident — which fits CAB thesis?

search_strategy.hit_criteria: Versioned release or config change with structured metadata and binary failure outcome (failed release, hotfix within 7d, or incident linked). ≥200 positive class preferred.

tasks.title: Industrial / safety-critical change control datasets
tasks.scope: Search aviation, NASA, manufacturing, energy — where formal change control exists and failures are recorded. Long shot but validates 'change control' is universal, not ITSM-specific.
acceptance_criteria: ≥3 sources investigated (NASA PRACA, NTSB maintenance-related, aviation MRO)
Honest feasibility note: likely too sparse or too domain-specific for CRBundle adapter
If nothing usable, document why in ≤1 paragraph (don't over-invest)

search_strategy.hit_criteria: Formal change/maintenance record paired with failure/incident outcome. Tier A/B. Expect low hit rate — task succeeds by documenting negative result quickly.

tasks.title: Academic paper data availability audit (cross-domain)
tasks.scope: Search papers that train on change→failure prediction across SE, ITSM, DevOps, process mining. Extract: private vs public, sample sizes, label method, whether authors share data on request.
acceptance_criteria: ≥15 papers catalogued (not just ArXiv ITSM 2023–2026)
Columns: authors, domain, n changes, n positives, label type, data URL, contact
ING/Kapel papers flagged for outreach
Papers claiming AUC >0.8 on private data listed as 'reference only' unless data found

search_strategy.hit_criteria: Paper explicitly predicts intervention failure with reported dataset size. Public supplementary data = immediate candidate. Private = reference + contact candidate.

tasks.title: Constructed dataset feasibility — multi-source temporal joins
tasks.scope: Evaluate whether we can BUILD a silver-tier dataset by joining public sources: GitHub (deployments, releases, merge commits) + incident issues + public postmortem corpora (postmortem.xyz, danlu/post-mortems) + status page archives.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture doc for construction: sources, join keys, time windows, expected label noise
Pilot scope defined: 1–2 repos (e.g., Kubernetes, HashiCorp) with rich incident history
Estimate: achievable n, person-days, API rate limits, license constraints
Sensitivity plan: window sizes (6h/24h/72h) and impact on positive-class count
Go/no-go recommendation with explicit failure modes

search_strategy.hit_criteria: Demonstrated join path yielding ≥100 silver-tier labeled interventions from public APIs/archives. Construction counts as hit even if no pre-packaged dataset exists.

tasks.title: Platform-wide keyword sweep (unbiased second pass)
tasks.scope: Re-run HuggingFace, Kaggle, GitHub, Zenodo with DOMAIN-NEUTRAL terms — deliberately excluding itsm/servicenow/change-management. Catch datasets v1 missed because labels use different vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria: Same platforms as v1 searched with new term lists — zero ITSM-specific keywords
≥20 datasets inspected (title + description), ≥3 new candidates not in v1 report
Deduped against research-1 through research-7 findings
Explicit confirmation: v1 ITSM-keyword search was subset of this broader search

search_strategy.hit_criteria: Any dataset with structured pre-action records + post-action failure labels passing Tier B or better. Semantic review required — reject agent benchmarks and pure incident-only logs.

tasks.title: Synthesis — tiered shortlist and validation roadmap
tasks.scope: Merge all task findings into docs/dataset-research-v2.md. Rank candidates WITHOUT defaulting to BPI 2014. Recommend validation strategy per project goal (architecture / predictive / full pipeline).
acceptance_criteria: Ranked shortlist with tier, n, stages covered, adapter effort, label quality
BPI 2014 position justified by evidence — not by incumbency
Recommended primary dataset per validation goal (may be different datasets for different goals)
Explicit 'will not work' section with structural reasons
Decision tree for user open questions
Updates docs/datasets.md and docs/evaluation.md cross-links

search_strategy.hit_criteria: Final deliverable: actionable recommendation the team can decide on in one review meeting
